forecaster_note: A few little peaky waves, best this morning for more south facing breaks. NE wind wave and traces of S swell for some peaky mixed up surf in the waist to chest range. Morning at the south facing spots and in the north corners is looking best as winds blow light northerly, before NE winds pick up mid-morning and it gets junky elsewhere. Saturday holds a similar small NE wind-swell; Sunday sees a stronger, gustier wind event push in with bigger surf at the exposed spots but onshore and lumpy — small clean corners the pick. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline

wind.summary: N ~24kph (35kph gusts) right now — offshore at Long Reef and Curl Curl, cross-shore at Dee Why and Manly. Onshore sea breeze fills in through the morning at most spots; best window is early.

days.note: Small NE wind-swell day — Long Reef and Curl Curl get the offshore morning window and the best ratings; Dee Why and Manly turn onshore earlier and stay the softest of the four.

dee-why.window: Best before 9am while it's still cross-shore and light — onshore sea breeze fills in and knocks it back to POOR by midday.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 46° ENE is inside your good window and wraps onto the Point's rights — take it frontside. Soft and paddle-heavy (thigh-chest); the near-dead-S groundswell underneath is too small to matter. Go early, it's onshore slop by lunch.

long-reef.window: Offshore all morning — best-rated spot on the coast today, holds shape until the wind swings cross-shore around midday.

tip.label: Best bet today
tip.text: Offshore N winds plus the day's top FAIR rating make Long Reef the standout — worth the drive for the cleanest walls on the Northern Beaches this morning.

swells.label: Secondary near-dead-S groundswell (wraps badly here, but small)

curl-curl.window: Offshore early (6-9am) before it swings cross-shore — a real live surf-cam read has it at 1-3ft right now, matching Long Reef for the morning session.

tip.label: Backside option
tip.text: Offshore at dawn and soaking up the same ENE wind-swell as Long Reef without the crowd — backside lefts in the crumble while it holds shape.

tip.label: Skip unless local

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Peaky, consistent, small-to-fun NE wind-swell — waist to chest at most spots. Winds are good for the AM with light NW'lies before turning onshore again.

dee-why.window: Short-period NE wind-swell holds waist-chest — offshore and clean early with light NW'lies before the sea breeze returns.

long-reef.window: Best-rated again — FAIR holds most of the day, offshore through the morning.

curl-curl.window: Offshore and consistent through the morning, FAIR most of the day.

manly.window: Improves to FAIR through the morning before the onshore sea breeze arrives midday.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday's covered in Tomorrow above — Sunday brings a stronger, gustier wind event: decent-to-overhead size at the south-facing exposures (Curl Curl, Dee Why, Manly) but onshore and lumpy; Long Reef's N corner stays smallest and cleanest. Sizes here are a 2-day-out estimate, not a measured forecast.

dee-why.window: A stronger, gustier wind event moves through — decent size at the exposures but onshore and lumpy; sheltered corners are the pick for a small clean wave.

long-reef.window: Sheltered N corner keeps it smallest and cleanest of the four as the onshore wind event fills in elsewhere.

curl-curl.window: South exposure picks up the most size of the four — head to overhead — but onshore and lumpy, best early if at all.

manly.window: Onshore and lumpy through most of the day — a small clean wave is possible in sheltered corners early.
